source_evidence.observation: The exercise asks: “Check that ∥ · ∥ψ2 is indeed a norm on the space of sub-gaussian random variables.”
A random variable X is called sub-gaussian when it satisfies one of the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) in Proposition 2.5.2.
The sub-gaussian norm is defined exactly by ∥X∥ψ2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2}; the preceding sentence describes it as the smallest K4 in property (iv).
For a random variable X, properties (i)–(iv) are equivalent, with their positive parameters differing by at most an absolute constant factor.
Property (iv) is the existence of K4 > 0 such that E exp(X²/K4²) ≤ 2.
The mean-zero assumption is introduced only for equivalence with the additional MGF property (v), not for properties (i)–(iv) used in Definition 2.5.6.

binders: X and Y range over the space of sub-gaussian random variables named in Exercise 2.5.7 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, anchor “on the space of sub-gaussian random variables”).
a ranges over the real scalars implicit in the surrounding real-random-variable context (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2(v), anchor “for all λ ∈ R”).
hypotheses: X and Y are sub-gaussian: each satisfies one of properties (i)–(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6, anchor “satisfies one of the equivalent properties i–iv”).
conclusions: The collection of sub-gaussian random variables is closed under the vector-space operations needed by the assertion that it is a normed space, in particular real scalar multiplication and addition (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7, anchor “a norm on the space”).
For every sub-gaussian X, the quantity ∥X∥ψ2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2} is finite and nonnegative (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13)).

Definiteness holds in the source’s intended equality convention: ∥X∥ψ2 = 0 if and only if X = 0 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7, anchor “is indeed a norm”; the equality convention is not locally specified).
Absolute homogeneity holds: ∥aX∥ψ2 = |a| ∥X∥ψ2 for every real scalar a (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7, anchor “is indeed a norm”).
The triangle inequality holds: ∥X + Y∥ψ2 ≤ ∥X∥ψ2 + ∥Y∥ψ2 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7, anchor “is indeed a norm”).
definitions_and_conventions: “Sub-gaussian random variable” means a random variable satisfying one of the equivalent properties (i)–(iv) in Proposition 2.5.2 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6).
The norm candidate is the exact gauge ∥X∥ψ2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2} (PDF page 16; printed page 27, equation (2.13)).
The threshold in the defining expectation bound is exactly 2, the scale t is strictly positive, and the exponent is X²/t² (PDF page 16; printed page 27, equation (2.13)).
Property (iv), to which the definition refers, requires some K4 > 0 satisfying E exp(X²/K4²) ≤ 2 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2(iv)).
implicit_context: The expectation E is taken with respect to the probability law of the random variable under discussion (PDF page 16; printed page 27, equation (2.13), anchor “E exp(X²/t²)”).
The surrounding section treats real random variables and real MGF parameters (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2(v), anchor “λ ∈ R”).

The singular phrase “the space of sub-gaussian random variables” implicitly requires X and Y to inhabit a common ambient probability space so that X + Y is defined, but that probability space is not named locally (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7).

No centering or independence assumption is imposed on Exercise 2.5.7: Definition 2.5.6 uses properties (i)–(iv), while Proposition 2.5.2 introduces E X = 0 only for property (v) (PDF page 13, printed page 24, and PDF page 16, printed page 27, anchors “Moreover, if E X = 0” and “properties i–iv”).

details: This is an exercise requesting verification of a norm assertion, not merely an equivalence up to absolute constants (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7, anchor “indeed a norm”).

The domain is the whole stated space of sub-gaussian random variables, defined through properties (i)–(iv), without a mean-zero restriction (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6; PDF page 13, printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2).
The asserted norm is the particular infimum functional in equation (2.13), with exponential-square integrability and threshold 2 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13)).
The phrase “indeed a norm” requires definiteness, absolute homogeneity, and the triangle inequality, together with a vector-space domain (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7).

Because the functional depends only on expectations, its definiteness is naturally sensitive only to almost-sure equality, although the local source passage does not state whether random variables are identified almost surely (PDF page 16; printed page 27, equation (2.13) and Exercise 2.5.7).

undebatable_constraints: The audited claim must concern the exact functional in equation (2.13), not merely a comparable moment, tail, or MGF quantity (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and Exercise 2.5.7).
The infimum is over t > 0 and the admissibility condition is exactly E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2 (PDF page 16; printed page 27, equation (2.13)).
The domain is the space of sub-gaussian random variables as defined through Proposition 2.5.2(i)–(iv) (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and Exercise 2.5.7).

The conclusion is a genuine norm assertion and therefore includes definiteness, exact absolute homogeneity, and the exact triangle inequality, not versions holding only up to absolute constant factors (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7, anchor “indeed a norm”).

No mean-zero hypothesis may be added: centering is required only for the additional property (v), whereas Definition 2.5.6 explicitly uses properties (i)–(iv) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2; PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6).
No independence hypothesis appears in the definition or exercise (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 and Exercise 2.5.7).

ambiguities.issue: The underlying probability space is not specified in the local statement.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7 says only “the space of sub-gaussian random variables,” and Definition 2.5.6 begins with “A random variable X,” without naming an ambient probability space.
ambiguities.impact: Addition X + Y and a single vector-space structure require the variables to be taken on a common probability space; a formal version must choose or bind that ambient space.

ambiguities.issue: The equality convention for random variables is not stated.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16; printed page 27, equation (2.13) defines the functional solely through expectation, while Exercise 2.5.7 calls it a norm without saying whether random variables are identified almost surely.
ambiguities.impact: On literal pointwise functions the functional cannot distinguish variables differing only on a null set, so definiteness gives a genuine norm naturally on almost-sure equivalence classes; without that quotient or an equivalent convention it is only a seminorm with respect to pointwise equality.

ambiguities.issue: The scalar field is not explicitly named in Exercise 2.5.7.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16; printed page 27, Exercise 2.5.7 says “a norm” without naming a field; the surrounding Proposition 2.5.2(v) on PDF page 13, printed page 24 quantifies λ ∈ R and treats X as a real random variable.
ambiguities.impact: The intended reading is a real normed space, but a formal statement must make the scalar field explicit.

ambiguities.issue: Definition 2.5.6 describes the value as the “smallest K4” and then defines it by an infimum over positive t.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6, anchors “the smallest K4 in property iv” and equation (2.13), “inf t > 0.”
ambiguities.impact: For the zero random variable every t > 0 is admissible, so there is no smallest positive admissible t although the infimum is 0; the displayed infimum formula must control the exact interpretation.

contracts.contract_plain_english: Exercise 2.5.7 asks for the exact quantity ∥X∥ψ2 = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X²/t²) ≤ 2} from Definition 2.5.6 to be proved a genuine norm on the full space of sub-gaussian random variables—those satisfying any of Proposition 2.5.2(i)–(iv)—with no centering or independence assumption (PDF page 16; printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6, equation (2.13), and Exercise 2.5.7; PDF page 13, printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2). Thus the claim entails closure of the domain, definiteness, real absolute homogeneity, and the triangle inequality. The local source leaves the ambient probability space, equality up to null sets, and scalar field implicit; almost-sure equality is consequential because the defining expectation cannot distinguish null-set modifications.
